The estate can recover full damages, including wrongful death and survival damages (medical expenses, pain and suffering, and lost earnings or support). The driver takes the victim as found, and a refusal of treatment based on sincere religious belief is generally not treated as unreasonable or as a superseding cause. The team note doesn't change this. Contributory negligence concerns the plaintiff's fault in causing the original accident. A later refusal of treatment falls under avoidable consequences (mitigation), which at most reduces damages and doesn't bar recovery. Courts also usually don't find a religiously motivated refusal unreasonable.
